problem: Determine the entry ${a}_{23}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix $A$ $=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}A=|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =3|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}|-0|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(1-0)-0+(-1-0) \\  & =3+0-1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since we want the entry ${a}_{23}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{32}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{32} & =(-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(0-1) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{23}^{′}=\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{32}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
